title: Elastic Quota Leases and Contention Mitigation PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As Dedicated customers scale up episodic workloads (batch inference, nightly indexing, or marketing surges), contention for reserved slots and prewarmed pools causes latency spikes and unpredictable throttling. Existing reservation semantics are rigid: tenants either have fully reserved slots or compete on best-effort. We need a graceful leasing mechanism and contention mitigation playbook that lets tenants borrow short-term quota, automatically negotiate headroom, and receive predictable fallbacks when capacity is constrained.

Goals:
- Provide an elastic lease primitive (short-term quota) that tenants can opt into for bursty workloads.
- Implement server-side contention mitigation policies that prioritize reserved allocations while offering bounded, auditable burst capacity to eligible tenants.
- Deliver operator tooling and console UX to visualize leases, revoke safely, and run post-incident reconciliation.
- Minimize tail latency regressions for high-priority tenants and keep cost transparency for customers.

Non-goals:
- Not a full replacement for long-term capacity reservations or committed contracts.
- Does not modify underlying kernel runtime batching; integration surfaces only control-plane allocation and routing rules.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Patel (Lead)
- Eng: Marco Ruiz (owner), Reliability team, Serving runtime team, Orchestration team
- Design: Priya Menon (console flows)
- Solutions/SE: Jess Huang (customer playbooks)
- Legal/Sales: consulted for contract language on soft leases

User personas & scenarios:
- Small PLG startup: Wants to handle traffic spikes during product launches without upgrading reserved tier.
- Enterprise media client: Executes nightly batch edits that briefly exceed reserved capacity and needs predictable, auditable borrowing behavior.
- Platform team: Wants safety guards to avoid noisy neighbors during peak windows and a simple rollback mechanism in incidents.

High-level solution:
1) Elastic Quota Lease (EQL) primitive: short-duration (configurable 5m–6h) lease that grants additional virtual slots drawn from a global or zonal burst pool. Leases are granted only if safety checks pass (headroom thresholds, priority class, recent misuse history).
2) Contention Mitigation Policies: combined policies that include: soft-priority decay, controlled preemption windows, and a staged fallback plan (model-variant downgrade -> quantized variant -> rate-limited responses).
3) Visibility & Controls: Console panel and APIs to request/inspect active leases, expected reclaim timelines, cost estimate of lease usage, and one-click emergency revoke.
4) Operator Playbook: procedures for diagnosing lease storms, revoking leases, rebalancing pools, and reconciling accounting (chargeback).

Core requirements:
- Requirements are phrased as must/have/should where applicable.
- EQL must support per-tenant configurable max-borrow (absolute tokens or percent of reserved capacity) and global policy caps.
- EQL must be auditable: every lease event must include requester, duration, policy applied, and a justification string.
- EQL must integrate with routing layer such that leased requests are tagged and can be routed to best-fit model variants.
- Contention Policy engine must support rules by tenant tier, label selectors, and recent usage heuristics (last 24h).
- Safety checks must include a fast path that denies leases if global headroom < X% (configurable) and a delayed path that can queue for prewarm if within Y minutes to expected free capacity.
- Console: request flow, approvals (auto/manual), telemetry chart (active leases, borrow rate, reclaimed), and historical ledger.
- Billing: metered lease usage exposed via usage API with separate line-item for billing.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria array)

Success metrics:
- 95th percentile request latency for reserved tenants during lease storms must not regress more than 10% vs baseline.
- Lease grant latency median < 200ms for fast-path, < 5s for queued prewarm path.
- Number of incidents attributable to uncontrolled cross-tenant bursts decreases by 60% in first 90 days.
- At least three large customers pilot EQL and provide positive feedback on predictability.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (experiment): API-only EQL available to internal tenants, no console. 2 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta): select customers opt-in, console visibility, billing line-item. 4 weeks.
- Phase 2 (GA): default for eligible tiers with safeguards and quota limits, operator playbook published. 6–8 weeks.

Operational runbooks & playbook links: see links field for draft docs.

Open questions:
- Pricing model: per-token vs time-based slot billing? (finance/commerce input needed)
- How to model cross-zone bursts with zonal headroom heterogeneity?
- What decay/backoff model minimizes churn when tenants repeatedly hit lease caps?

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Abuse by tenants to avoid committed capacity - Mitigation: debt ledger, hard caps, contract language, and automated throttles.
- Risk: Complexity in routing - Mitigation: phased integration and strict tagging of leased traffic.

References & artifacts: drive doc (design spec), draft console mocks, prototype PRs, telemetry dashboard queries listed in links.
acceptance_criteria: EQL API: create/read/list/cancel endpoints exist and pass automated contract tests
Grant decision latency: median < 200ms for fast-path in synthetic tests
Policy enforcement: when global headroom < configured threshold, new EQL grants are denied or queued per policy
Audit trail: all lease events visible in console ledger and match backend logs for at least 90 days
Routing tag: leased traffic is tagged and routed to configured model-variant fallback chain
Billing: usage exported as line-item in usage API for billing reconciliation
Console UX: request flow and revoke button present in beta with role-based visibility
Operator playbook: runbook tested with oncall during simulated lease storm and resulting remediation steps document updated
Performance SLO: reserved-tenant p95 latency regression <= 10% under controlled burst test
